correctness.rationale: First-return U A D B with the marked up-step gives F=yC(y)^2/(1+xyC(y)+x^2 C(x)) in F_2[[x,y]]. In characteristic two Catalan C=1+z^2 C^2 and uniqueness imply C(z)=sum_a z^(2^(a+1)-2). Multiplication verifies (x+y)F=xy C(x)C(y)+C(y)+1. Diagonal and swapped off-diagonal monomials divided by x+y yield exactly I_n when n+1 has one or two binary bits, and none otherwise; binary expansion uniqueness avoids overlap. Expanding product (1-2u_t) modulo 4 yields W_n(b)=C_n-2 sum_{t in I_n}b_t. Legendre gives nu2(C_n)=s2(n+1)-1. For digit sums 1,2,3, W_n(0)=C_n establishes sharp gcd valuations and half the characters with W=2 (mod4) for sum 2. Independence from finite evidence: a separate path enumeration and Walsh transform checked every character for n=1..7; the universal conclusion follows from the algebra, not tests.
residual_risks: The bound for even Catalan numbers does not prove nonvanishing or invertibility; exact nullities and higher dyadic layers not asserted.
Finite tests only through n=7 independently; all-length algebra checked symbolically by the displayed formal identity.

value.rationale: Uniform binary-position parity of Catalan matroid bases is a structural combinatorial law, not a renamed Catalan count. It gives every Walsh coefficient modulo four at once for arbitrary semilength and immediate sharp nontrivial dyadic obstructions and rank information. This is mathematically useful for finite Boolean convolution even though it does not solve higher layers or exact rank.
residual_risks: Value is restricted to mod-four information; exact ranks at higher-digit sums remain unknown.

limitations: No assertion of exact zero set, exact convolution rank outside the stated cases, odd gcd factors or dyadic layers above four.
